m:vieille: Free to walk around at any time. The shops are open Monday to Saturday and almost all closed on Sundays (as everywhere in Switzerland); cafés and restaurants stay open.
m:cattedrale: Hours from a guide (Routard), not the official website: to be confirmed. From October to May the cathedral opens Monday to Saturday 10am–5:30pm and Sunday noon–5:30pm; the towers close half an hour earlier. The nave is free, the tower climb costs CHF 7 (about €7.50). The archaeological site is paid (check price and hours on site-archeologique.ch).
m:bastions: The park and the wall are free and open at any time. The giant chess sets can be used freely when there's no snow.
m:rade: The promenade is free. The jet stops in strong wind or frost and every autumn it's turned off for about five weeks for maintenance: in 2025 it was off from 29 October to 21 November; I couldn't find the 2026 dates, so check on sig-ge.ch before going.
m:paquis: Winter season from 20 September 2026 to 23 May 2027 (from the baths' website): entry to the baths costs CHF 2; the wellness area (sauna, hammam, Turkish bath) is open Monday 9am–10:30pm, Tuesday–Friday 9am–9:30pm (Tuesday women only), Saturday 9am–10:30pm, Sunday 8am–10:30pm, and costs CHF 22 (CHF 15 on Mondays). Whether you need the entry ticket just to walk on the jetty: to be confirmed.
m:mah: From the City of Geneva website: Tuesday–Sunday 11am–6pm, Thursday noon–9pm, closed Monday. The permanent collections should be free and temporary exhibitions paid, but the information comes from a 2014 listing: to be confirmed on the museum website. An extension and restoration project for the building is under way, with no dates.
m:patek: From the museum website: Tuesday–Friday and Sunday 2–6pm, Saturday 10am–6pm, closed Monday. Entry CHF 10 (about €10.70). The website lists some closures on public holidays (for example 25 December): check the dates before going.
m:croce: Hours from a museums.ch listing (the museum website says until 6pm): to be confirmed. Tuesday–Sunday 10am–5pm, Thursday until 8pm, closed Monday; closed on 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January. Ticket CHF 15 (about €16.10), reduced CHF 10. From July 2026 the museum is undergoing works for almost two years but stays open: the new permanent exhibition opens in stages (first part in October 2026, «future» section in December 2026) and will be complete on 8 May 2028.
m:onu: The tour costs CHF 25 (about €26.80) for adults, CHF 22 for students and seniors, CHF 14 for ages 14–17; book online on the UN Geneva website. Tickets for individual visitors are released on the 20th of each month for the following month and sell out fast. You need valid ID (a European ID card is fine) and must arrive 30 minutes early. The palace is being renovated: the route may change and access may close at short notice. Tour days and times aren't given on the page: I've assumed weekday mornings and afternoons, to be confirmed when booking.
m:cern: From the CERN website: open Tuesday to Sunday, closed Monday; exhibitions from 9am to 5pm (last entry 4:30pm). Free entry; guided lab tours must be booked. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December and 1 January. The tram ride from Cornavin takes about 35 minutes (estimate, check on tpg.ch).
m:carouge: Free to walk around. The market on Place du Marché is on Wednesday and Saturday mornings, about 8am–1pm (from a 2015 listing: to be confirmed). It takes about 20 minutes by tram 12 or 18.
vd:soleil: The neighbourhood café most famous for fondue, in Petit-Saconnex, a little outside the centre: a rustic place where you eat moitié-moitié cheese fondue with a glass of white wine. Very popular with Genevans, often full in the evening.
vp:soleil: A fondue usually costs CHF 28–35 per person (estimate, menu not seen). Hours differ between two sources (Time Out and a fondue guide): I've used the more cautious ones, to be confirmed. Best to book for dinner.
vd:cousine: Roast chicken with potatoes and salad, in a large simple room on the oldest square in the Old Town: food for everyone, quick and generous, with oven-baked chips and the house sauce.
vp:cousine: Half a chicken with potatoes and salad costs about CHF 18 (about €19); full meals CHF 15–20 (menu not seen, from a 2014 listing and a more recent guide). Hours from a 2014 listing: to be confirmed.
vd:armures: A restaurant in the 17th-century building next to the cathedral, with suits of armour on the walls: fondue, raclette and Genevan dishes served in a mountain-tavern atmosphere. It's touristy, but historic, and handy after visiting St-Pierre.
vp:armures: Fondue starts at CHF 26 per person (about €28); a main course usually costs CHF 25–40 (menu not seen). Hours from Time Out, to be confirmed.
vd:buvette: The Bains des Pâquis restaurant on the lake: a simple, excellent dish of the day, coffee and cakes, and in winter moitié-moitié fondue. Eat inside or, when it's sunny, outside on the jetty.
vp:buvette: The dish of the day costs about CHF 15 (about €16) and winter fondue about CHF 25 (about €27), from a guide (menu not seen). Hours vary between guides (from 7 or 8am, until 10:30 or 11pm): I've used the more cautious ones, to be confirmed.
vd:papon: A historic Old Town café with high ceilings, mirrors and wooden tables: breakfast, coffee, something savoury at lunch and an aperitif in the evening. A good place to stop out of the cold.
vp:papon: Main courses cost CHF 30–40, but a coffee with a slice of cake or a sandwich costs much less (menu not seen). Hours from Time Out: to be confirmed.
vd:beyrouth: A Lebanese place between Cornavin and the lake: meat shawarma with plenty of garlic sauce (toum), falafel and quick sandwiches, good and cheap for Geneva. Ideal for a quick lunch, standing or seated.
vp:beyrouth: A sandwich or a quick dish usually costs CHF 10–18 (estimate from a guide, menu not seen). According to the guide it closes at 2am (Friday and Saturday at 4am); here I've put midnight to be safe, to be confirmed.
vd:fornello: A Neapolitan pizzeria with a wood-fired oven near Cornavin, for when after days of fondue you fancy a margherita. Book in the evening.
vp:fornello: A pizza usually costs CHF 20–28 (estimate, menu not seen). Open Monday to Saturday for lunch and dinner, closed on Sundays, from an online guide: to be confirmed.
vd:edelweiss: The Hotel Edelweiss restaurant, decorated like a mountain chalet, near the station: fondue and raclette served in the evening, in a very touristy but cheerful atmosphere.
vp:edelweiss: Fondue usually costs CHF 30–40 per person (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from a fondue guide (Tuesday–Saturday 6–11pm): to be confirmed.
cd:lago: An hour on the lake by boat, with views of the Jet d'eau and the Alps.
cd:reformation: The story of Calvin and the Reformation, next to the cathedral.
cd:saleve: A cable car up the mountain above Geneva, in France: views of the lake and Mont Blanc.
cx:saleve: It's in France, about 8 km from the centre. Bring your ID.
cd:ariana: Ceramics and glass in a palace next to the Palais des Nations.
cd:barbier: Art and objects from Africa, Oceania and pre-Columbian America.
